subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted Slack transport, or by changing Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured gap is mostly outside OpenClaw code, but steering docs or defaults changes Slack onboarding expectations and deployment requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the local/private-ingress default and make Slack docs or setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Sponsor a larger Slack setup/default change that nudges new hosted installs away from Socket Mode, with explicit upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the current deployment-shape transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no latency-specific guidance is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the local/private-ingress default and make Slack docs or setup guidance explicitly prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They produced the measurement, merged the current-main partial fix, and scoped the remaining follow-up to HTTP-mode guidance.
